title: 材料科学Ⅲ
subtitle: Materials Science III
keywords: Corrosion and Protection 2.Fracture mechanics 3.Alloyed steel and non-ferrous materials 4.Non-metallic materials and Composite materials 5.Material seliction
educationalGoal: In the design and manufacture of machines and structures, it is necessary to select appropriate materials based on an understanding of their properties. Based on the basic knowledge of the structure and properties of materials acquired in Materials Science I and II, students learn corrosion and fracture mechanisms, which are defects of materials, and understand the structure and properties of nonferrous metals, resins, ceramics, and composite materials. Furthermore, students discuss some cases of material selection and it helps deeper understanding of materials.
advice: The following items are studied. -Corrosion and corrosion protection techniques -Fracture mechanics -Stainless steel and alloyed steel -Aluminum and aluminum alloys -Copper and copper alloys -Plastics -Ceramics -Composite materials Some case studies of material selection based on Ishikawa area are discussed in order to understand materials knowledge deeper. Lectures are conducted by face-to-face teaching, also can be took place by remote class depending on a situation.
requiredKnowledge: This lecture requires the understanding of Materials Science I and Materials Science II. Students should understand the relationship between microstructure and material properties in Materials Science I,and also understand the relationship between microstructure formation and properties of steel in Materials Science Ⅱ. Knowledge of thermodynamics is also required to understand corrosion mechanisms.

activityGoals.body: Abilities to understand the basic mechanisms of corrosion, typical corrosion forms and corrosion control methods
Abilities to understand the failure mechanisms of materials.
Abilities to understand the properties of stainless steel and alloyed steels.
Abilities to understand the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resigns, composite materials.
Abilities to select appropriate materials according to engineering needs.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) Abilities to understand the basic principle of corrosion and typical corrosion forms, and corrosion protection methods. 2) Abilities to be able to explain the failure mechanism of materials. 3) Abilities to understand the characteristics of advanced steel materials such as alloyed steel and stainless steels. 4)Abilities to be able to explain the relationship between the structure and the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resins and composite materials. 5)Abilities to be able to select appropriate materials using the knowledge acquired in this course.
achievementLevels.standard: 1) Abilities to understand that corrosion progresses by the anode reaction and cathode reaction and to explain the principle of cathodic protection. 2) Abilities to be able to explain the meaning of the plane strain fracture toughness value (KIC). 3)Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of advanced materials such as alloy steel and stainless steels. 4) Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of typical aluminum and copper alloys, ceramics, resins and composite materials. 5) Abilities to be able to point out the hazards of materials in the environment in which they are used.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the educational objectives and achievements of this course. To understand the role of materials in the field of engineering. To explain the lecture policy of this course. To review the contents of Materials Science I and Materials Science II.
lessons.assignments: To review the contents of Materials Science I and Materials Science II using the textbook and handouts. Understand the educational objectives of this course.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the principle of corrosion which include anodic reaction and cathodic reaction, and polarization phenomenon. To understand the effects of pH and electric potential on corrosion reactions.
lessons.assignments: Students should review the oxidizing and reducing reactions involving the transfer of electrons studied in high school.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the characteristics and principles of uniform attack, which are typical forms of corrosion. To understand the hazardous material conditions depending on the environment.
lessons.assignments: To observe the corrosion forms everyday metal products such as cars, coins, and cookware.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the characteristics and principles of typical forms of corrosion (pitting and galvanic corrosion). To understand the hazardous material conditions depending on surrounding environments.
lessons.assignments: To explain the corrosion mechanisms of everyday metal products such as cars, coins, and cookware.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the fracture mechanisms originating from micro-cracks.
lessons.assignments: To explain the methods of corrosion protection for everyday metal products.

lessons.content: [Quiz 1] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 1 to lecture 5. [Lecture] To understand the properties of alloy steels and stainless steels in terms of their structure.
lessons.assignments: To review of the contents of lectures 1 to lecture 5. To review the strengthening mechanisms of metals such as dislocation strengthening, solid solution strengthening, and precipitation strengthening.

lessons.content: [Review and Self-reflection] Quiz 1 is explained and questions are asked to clear up the contents of the lectures. [Lecture] To understand the different types of copper alloys and their structure and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review the relationship between the microstructure formed from the eutectoid system state diagram and the properties of the obtained material.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of Cu alloys and their structures, and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review the precipitation strengthening by aging and the sliding deformation mechanism by transition.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of Al alloys and magnesium alloys, their structures, and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review the three types of chemical bonds and their characteristics.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of ceramics and their structures and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review of basic crystal structures such as fcc and bcc and their characteristics

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of composite materials and their structure and characteristics.

[Quiz 2] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 6 to lecture 11. [Overall lecture] Discussions on examples of material selection deepen confirmation of obtained knowledge and understanding of materials.
lessons.assignments: To review of the contents of lectures 6 to lecture 11.

lessons.content: [Review and Self-reflection] Quiz 2 is explained and questions are asked to clear up the contents of the lectures. [Overall lecture] Discussions on examples of material selection deepen confirmation of obtained knowledge and understanding of materials.
lessons.operation: Commentary on Quiz 1 Lecture Q&A Case study
lessons.assignments: To think about the reasons for the selection of everyday metal product.

lessons.content: [Final examination] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 1 to lecture 13. [Overall lecture] Discussions on examples of material selection deepen confirmation of obtained knowledge and understanding of materials.

[Review and Self-reflection] Final examination is explained and questions are asked to clear up the contents of the lectures. Discussion and explanation of the report assignment. Students will deepen their overall understanding of Materials Science I, Materials Science II, and this course.
